subject: E2E tail-probing plan for hosted vs incumbent — next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Aaron Chen <aaron@novusai.com>, NovusAI SRE team <sre@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: E2E tail-probing plan for hosted vs incumbent — next steps

Thanks for the call today — good alignment on what matters for NovusAI. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the latency qualification probe (p95/p99 end-to-end) comparing Redwood hosted API to your current provider. I focused this plan on measurable deliverables and minimal ops friction.

High-level targets (from today's discussion):
- p95 target: <= 200 ms (interactive search use case)
- p99 target: <= 450 ms
- Sustained concurrency envelope: 1, 5, 20, 50, 200 RPS per tenant (we'll map to your peak/normal buckets)
- Streaming requirement: server-sent events for incremental tokens; target streaming tail similar to non-streamed request for p95 (allowing small additional overhead)

Planned phases (3):
1) Microbench (cloud): single-tenant, repeated small payloads to validate raw serving kernel latency and quantized model variants.
2) Replay (shadow): replay sample traffic from NovusAI (anonymized) through Redwood hosted endpoints to capture end-to-end latencies with real request shapes.
3) Hybrid shadow: inject small % of live traffic (shadow) and run 1-hour soak at target concurrency points to observe tail behavior and routing effects.

Instrumentation we need from NovusAI:
- Representative trace file (pcap or trace events) for representative peak window — thanks for offering earlier.
- Sample payloads (size distribution) and typical prefix lengths for streaming requests.
- A short-lived API key for Redwood test runner or signed URL for replay.

Redwood deliverables:
- Measurement matrix (we'll attach a CSV template) with p50/p95/p99 plus request-size buckets and percentiles for token count.
- Clear runbook that separates network-only vs model-serving latency (we'll correlate with your Kibana dashboard).
- Test artifacts: histograms, time-series, server traces, and a short write-up on potential mitigations (batching profiles, KV cache warmups, routing fallbacks).

Next steps / asks: please confirm the traffic window you'd like us to replay (e.g., Oct 8 13:00–14:00 PDT), and share the sample trace. I've attached a first-draft test plan (redwood_latencypoc_test_plan_v1.xlsx) — suggest we iterate on that.

If that all looks good, we'll schedule the microbench run on Wed and the shadow replay the following week.

Thanks,
Olga
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_latencypoc_test_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet: phases, metrics, runbook)

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 4:12 PM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks for the call today — good alignment on what matters for NovusAI. Quick recap...

Thanks Olga — this looks right. A few clarifications from our side before you start:
- Our current provider numbers (measured at the app layer) are roughly p95 ~ 180 ms, p99 ~ 420–500 ms depending on traffic spikes; the p99 variability is what keeps us up at night.
- We do request-side batching during peak windows (we aggregate short queries in 5–10 ms windows) which helps under bursty load; please account for that when replaying.
- Attached is a sample trace from Oct 4 (novus_sample_trace_20261004.pcap). It covers a 15-minute peak window with a mix of streaming and non-streaming traffic.

We are comfortable with the Oct 8 window for replay. We'll also create a short-lived replay API key tied to our staging org (will send via separate secure channel).

One ask: can Redwood provide a single-dashboard artifact we can drop into our Kibana (CSV/JSON) so we can directly compare lines?

Aaron
Head of Platform, NovusAI

Attachment stubs: novus_sample_trace_20261004.pcap (pcap: 15-minute peak trace)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aaron Chen <aaron@novusai.com>, NovusAI SRE team <sre@novusai.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: E2E tail-probing plan for hosted vs incumbent — test methodology

Thanks Aaron / Olga — quick note on how we'll measure to keep things apples-to-apples. Proposed measurement methodology:

Measurement phases (detail):
- Microbench: 1:v1 model, no batching, repeated cold and warm runs to capture kernel-level behavior. We'll log server kernel latency + TCP handshake.
- Replay: we will replay NovusAI trace 1:1 (timestamps normalized) with option to preserve batching behavior. We'll run at 0.5x, 1x, and 2x of the observed traffic envelope.
- Hybrid shadow: 0.5% of live traffic shadowed for 1 hour at target concurrency points (safe mode).

Instrument requirements (from Redwood):
- We will add X-Request-Id and propagate trace headers so you can join traces in Kibana.
- We'll export per-request metrics to CSV and a prometheus-style histogram (buckets) so you can overlay directly.
- For streaming, we'll capture both first-byte latency and completion latency; p95/p99 will be captured on completion latency but we'll also report streaming token-latency distribution.

Concurrency grid we'll run (per-tenant): 1, 5, 20, 50, 200. For each point we'll run 5-minute steady-state and a 10-minute spike run.

Pre-reqs for NovusAI: please enable short-term replay key and confirm CIDR for inbound test traffic (we'll white-list). Also if possible provide a small sample of typical batching windows (ms).

I'll take ownership of run orchestration. Marissa — can you prepare the CSV template and a short dashboard JSON we can hand to Aaron?

Ben
Sr Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- Thu Oct 14: Hybrid shadow (0.5% live) — brief soak at 50 RPS for 1 hour.

If there are no objections I'll lock the schedule and kick off the microbench tomorrow morning.

Olga
